title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding is a process used to convert categorical data into a binary matrix. Each category is represented by a column, and a row has a $$1$$ in the column corresponding to its category and 0s elsewhere.

title: Analyzing the Design Matrix
text: Look at the design matrix. Each row represents a data point, and each column (except the intercept) represents a category of the categorical feature.

title: Counting Unique Categories
text: Count the number of columns (excluding the intercept) that have a $$1$$ in at least one row. This will give you the number of unique categories.

title: Determine the Number of Unique Categories
text: How many columns (excluding the intercept) have a $$1$$ in at least one row?

title: Considering the Zero Rows
text: Rows $$5$$ and $$6$$ have all zeros in the one-hot encoded columns. This indicates an additional category not represented by a specific column.

title: Final Count of Unique Categories
text: Add the number of columns with a $$1$$ to account for the category represented by the zero rows.
